chapter: Teachers: Preston Jackson and Roy Palmer
title: Roy Palmer on records and High Society
summary: Wynn and the interviewer discuss Palmer's reputation and whether he recorded with Jelly Roll Morton or played the High Society clarinet solo.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Remembering Jelly Roll Morton: the man, the band

blocks.x: You know, Jolly Roe Martin and his Library of Congress records, he did a lot of talking and playing and, too. And he said Roy was his favorite trombonist. He said he was the greatest they had in New Orleans in the old days, too.
Roy was definitely one of the greatest. I understand that he made a... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ...
Okay, do you want to finish that up?
Okay, you were saying something about this record? Did Roy make it?
Yeah, Roy made a record, I understand, with Jelly Roll. I've never had to hear the record of High Society with Roy playing the Picou's clarinet solo. No, I don't think he did that. On the trombone.
No, I don't think he did that. No?

Well, there is supposed to be such a record that was made. Now, I know Roy can play it because he has played it for me. Lee Collins played it too on the trumpet. Yeah, well, it would be much easier on the trumpet, but on the trombone, that is something. Roy has played that This is Pretty. And there was a record, I remember at the time that it was made, maybe it didn't even come out or something, but I remember the...
